content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a Luke 2:48-49 challenge by saying Mary's phrase is immediately qualified by the child's next phrase, which is a verse-by-verse treatment of pressed witnesses rather than a chain-against-chain footing analysis.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"\"never verse by verse\": I weighed whether the judge may qualify one pressed verse with the next verse as part of assessing a link, or whether K-C requires the collision to be weighed only as chain against chain by footing; I read K-C to require the latter.","why":"The judge uses a one-verse qualification of Luke 2:48 by Luke 2:49 instead of weighing the pressed chain against the link by footing, so it does the verse-by-verse move K-C forbids."}
